'''Brandon Davies''' (born July 25, 1991) is an American-born naturalized Ugandan<ref>[https://sportando.basketball/en/brandon-davies-receives-ugandan-passport/ Brandon Davies receives Ugandan passport.]</ref> former professional [[basketball]] player. He represented the senior [[Ugandan national basketball team|Ugandan national team]]. He was an all-conference college player at [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|Brigham Young University]]. Davies is a two time [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague]] selection.

==Early life and college career==
Davies was born in [[Philadelphia]], Pennsylvania but adopted by single mother Kathy Davies and raised in [[Provo, Utah]].<ref name="NYT">{{cite news |author=Branch |first=John |authorlink=John Branch (journalist) |date=March 12, 2011 |title=Kept Off Court, but Welcomed by B.Y.U. Fans and Teammates |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/03/13/sports/ncaabasketball/13byu.html}}</ref> He attended [[Provo High School]], where his team won state titles in his sophomore and junior seasons. After considering schools such as [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]], [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], and [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]], Davies chose to play [[college basketball]] at [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|Brigham Young]].<ref name=BYU>{{cite web | title =Brandon Davies BYU athletic profile | publisher =BYUCougars.com | url =http://byucougars.com/athlete/m-basketball/brandon-davies | access-date =June 23, 2013 | archive-date =July 12, 2013 | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20130712232022/http://byucougars.com/athlete/m-basketball/brandon-davies | url-status =dead }}</ref>

After playing a reserve role as a freshman in [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10]], Davies became a key player for the Cougars as a sophomore. He served as the key inside player for the small, sharp-shooting [[2010–11 BYU Cougars men's basketball team|2010–11 Cougars]] (led by eventual National Player of the Year [[Jimmer Fredette]]). BYU raced to a 27–2 record and was ranked no. 3 in the [[AP Poll]] when Davies was suspended from the team for violating [[BYU Honor Code|BYU's honor code]] by having [[premarital sex]] with his girlfriend.<ref name=NYT/>

Davies was reinstated to the team as a junior and was named to the All-[[West Coast Conference]] team in each of his last two seasons at BYU. As a senior, Davies served as team captain and averaged 17.7 [[Points per game|points]] and 8.0 [[rebounds per game]].<ref name=BYU/>

==Professional career==
Following his graduation from BYU, Davies was invited to participate in the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]] (PIT) pre-[[NBA draft]] camp. Davies performed well, averaging 20.7 points per game on 68% shooting and grabbing 9.3 rebounds per game. He was named MVP of the PIT.<ref>{{cite news |last=Reheuser |first=Rob |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Davies finishes up strong at Portsmouth Invitational |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/04/14/day-four-portsmouth-invitational-tournament/index.html |url-status=dead |access-date=June 24, 2013 |archive-date=June 22, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130622141544/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/04/14/day-four-portsmouth-invitational-tournament/index.html }}</ref> Davies' performance earned him an invitation to the Chicago [[NBA draft combine]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865579764/BYU-basketball-Brandon-Davies-receives-invite-to-NBA-draft-combine-in-Chicago.html?pg=all |title=BYU basketball: Brandon Davies receives invite to NBA draft combine in Chicago |last=Call |first=Jeff |date=May 10, 2013 |work=The Deseret News |url-status=dead |access-date=June 24, 2013 |archive-date=June 22, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130622152404/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865579764/BYU-basketball-Brandon-Davies-receives-invite-to-NBA-draft-combine-in-Chicago.html?pg=all }}</ref> After going undrafted in the [[2013 NBA draft]], he joined the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.ksl.com/?sid=25790451&nid=498 |title=Undrafted Davies will play for the Clippers in Summer League |first=Jason |last=Shepherd |date=June 28, 2013 | work=ksl.com}}</ref> On September 5, 2013, he signed with the Clippers,<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-sign-brandon-davies|title=Clippers Sign Brandon Davies|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=September 5, 2013|access-date=December 13, 2014}}</ref> but was later waived on October 21.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14597|title=Clippers waive forward Brandon Davies|work=insidehoops.com|date=October 21, 2013|access-date=December 13, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141211081301/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14597|archive-date=December 11, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2013–2014)===
On October 28, 2013, Davies signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/philadelphia/news/sixers-sign-rookie-free-agent-brandon-davies |title=Sixers Sign Rookie Free Agent Brandon Davies |date=October 28, 2013 | work=cbsnews.com |access-date=May 15, 2023}}</ref> He played in his first NBA game on November 2, 2013, against the [[Chicago Bulls]], scoring two points in two minutes of action. On January 18, 2014, he fractured his right small finger, requiring surgery and up to a month of rehabilitation.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.delawareonline.com/story/posting-up/2014/02/06/davies-has-surgery-on-fractured-finger-out-at-least-a-month/4784563|title= Davies has surgery on fractured finger, out at least a month |last=Wolf |first=Jason |work=delawareonline.com|date=February 6, 2014|access-date=May 15, 2023}}</ref>

On November 5, 2014, Davies scored a career-high 20 points in an 89–91 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400578350|title=Tobias Harris' jumper at buzzer lifts Magic to first win of season|work=ESPN|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=November 5, 2014|agency=Associated Press|access-date=December 13, 2014}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2014–2015)===
On December 11, 2014, Davies was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Andrei Kirilenko]], [[Jorge Gutiérrez (basketball)|Jorge Gutiérrez]], the Nets' second-round draft pick in [[2020 NBA draft|2020]], the right to swap second-round picks in [[2018 NBA draft|2018]], and cash considerations.<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/nets-acquire-brandon-davies|title=Nets Acquire Brandon Davies|last=Sapp|first=Demetris|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=December 11, 2014|access-date=May 15, 2023}}</ref> On January 6, 2015, he was waived by the Nets after appearing in seven games.<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/brooklyn-nets-waive-brandon-davies|title=Brooklyn Nets Waive Brandon Davies|last=Plonchak|first=Kyle|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=January 6, 2015|access-date=May 15, 2023}}</ref>

===Élan Chalon (2015)===
On January 12, 2015, Davies signed with [[Élan Chalon]] of the [[Ligue Nationale de Basket|LNB]] Pro League in [[Chalon-sur-Saône]], France for the rest of the [[2014–15 LNB Pro A season]] as a replacement for an injured player.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/148312/brandon-davies-signs-with-elan-chalon.html|title=Brandon Davies signs with Elan Chalon|work=Sportando.com|date=January 12, 2015|access-date=January 12, 2015}}</ref> He helped Élan reach the league playoffs.

===Pallacanestro Varese (2015–2016)===
In August 2015, Davies signed with [[Pallacanestro Varese]] in [[Varese]], Italy for the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.pallacanestrovarese.it/brandon-davies-nuovo-acquisto-di-pallacanestro-varese/ |title=Brandon Davies, nuovo acquisto di Pallacanestro Varese |access-date=2019-07-04 |archive-date=2019-07-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190704231824/http://www.pallacanestrovarese.it/brandon-davies-nuovo-acquisto-di-pallacanestro-varese/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===AS Monaco (2016–2017)===
In July 2016, Davies signed with [[AS Monaco Basket|AS Monaco]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]] and the [[Basketball Champions League]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.bebasket.fr/championnat-pro-a/brandon-davies-vers-monaco.html |title="Brandon Davies vers Monaco" on BEBasket |access-date=2016-07-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160703105040/http://www.bebasket.fr/championnat-pro-a/brandon-davies-vers-monaco.html |archive-date=2016-07-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Žalgiris Kaunas (2017–2019)===
[[File:Brandon Davies 0 BC Žalgiris EuroLeague 20180223.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Davies with [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] in 2018]]
In the summer of 2017, Davies played in [[The Basketball Tournament]] on [[ESPN]] for Team Fredette. He competed for the $2 million prize, and for Team Fredette, he scored 20 points and grabbed seven rebounds in their first-round game, which they lost to Team Utah (Utah Alumni) 100–97.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bracket {{!}} The Basketball Tournament |url=https://www.thetournament.com/bracket |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190514091135/https://www.thetournament.com/bracket |archive-date=2019-05-14 |access-date=2018-02-27 |website=thetournament.com |language=en}}</ref>

On June 23, 2017, Davies signed with a 1+1 contract with Lithuanian team [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/lithuania/238307/zalgiris-kaunas-signs-brandon-davies-to-a-1-1-deal.html|title=Zalgiris Kaunas signs Brandon Davies to a 1+1 deal|work=Sportando.com|date=June 23, 2017|access-date=June 23, 2017}}</ref> Over his two seasons with Žalgiris, Davies helped the team achieve much success, in particular in the EuroLeague. On May 9, 2019, Davies was named to the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]], becoming the first Žalgiris player to win the award in 15 years since [[Arvydas Sabonis]] in [[2003–04 Euroleague|2004]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2018-19 All-EuroLeague First Team presented by 7DAYS|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/2018-19-all-euroleague-first-team-presented-by-7days/|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]|date=May 9, 2019|access-date=July 23, 2026}}</ref>

===FC Barcelona (2019–2022)===
On July 4, 2019, Davies signed a two-year deal with the Spanish club [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Barcelona brings All-EuroLeague center Davies aboard |url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9quiiqc5i6mwpgy7 |access-date=4 July 2019 |work=EuroLeague.net |date=4 July 2019}}</ref> In his second game with Barcelona, Davies recorded 24 points and 11 rebounds in a 95–87 win over [[Saski Baskonia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Spain/2019/0929_100_108.asp|title=Saski Baskonia 87 – FC Barcelona Basquet 95|publisher=EuroBasket|date=September 29, 2019|access-date=June 29, 2020}}</ref>

===Olimpia Milano (2022–2023)===
On June 24, 2022, Davies signed a two-year contract with Italian champions [[Olimpia Milano]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]], playing also the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Milan signs star center Davies|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/milan-signs-davies/|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]|date=June 24, 2022|access-date=July 5, 2023}}</ref> On July 5, 2023, Davies mutually parted ways with the Italian powerhouse.

===Valencia (2023–2024)===
On July 5, 2023, Davies signed a two-year deal with Spanish club [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Valencia signs Brandon Davies to two-year deal|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/valencia-basket-signs-brandon-davies-to-multi-year-deal/|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]|date=July 5, 2023|access-date=July 5, 2023}}</ref> On July 4, 2024, he parted ways with the club.

===Partizan Belgrade (2024–2025)===
On August 20, 2024, Davies signed with [[KK Partizan|Partizan Mozzart Bet]] of the [[ABA League]], [[Basketball League of Serbia]] (KLS) and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Crno-bela simfonija: Nova energija i duh tradicije Partizana na ulasku u sezonu 2024-25|url=https://partizan.basketball/vesti/aktuelno/3738|website=Partizan.basketball|date=August 20, 2024|access-date=August 20, 2024|language=Serbian |last1=Normasoft. Net |first1=Normasoft }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Geoff|last=Gillingham|title=Partizan adds Brandon Davies at center|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/kk-partizan-adds-brandon-davies-at-center/|website=EuroLeagueBasketball.net|date=August 19, 2024|access-date=August 19, 2024}}</ref> In his debut season with Partizan, Davies averaged 9.9 points and 3.6 rebounds over 33 EuroLeague games, while shooting career-high 49.2% from the three-point line. During the season, Partizan managed to lift the record eighth [[2024–25 ABA League First Division|ABA League]] championship, and the [[2024–25 Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]] championship, the first one after 11 seasons.

===Alvark Tokyo (2025–2026)===
On June 27, 2025, Davies signed with [[Alvark Tokyo]] of the [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Announcement of Brandon Davis' new contract for the 2025-26 season|url=https://www.alvark-tokyo.jp/news/detail/team/id=20425|website=alvark-tokyo.jp|date=June 27, 2025|access-date=July 13, 2025}}</ref> His campaign was cut short by injuries, limiting him to 25 games during the [[2025–26 B1 League season|2025–26]] season where averaged 13.4 points and 4.8 rebounds.

On July 23, 2026, Davies announced his retirement from professional basketball.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brandon Davies announces sudden retirement from professional basketball|url=https://basketnews.com/news-252482-brandon-davies-announces-sudden-retirement-from-professional-basketball.html|website=basketnews.com|date=July 23, 2026|access-date=July 23, 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
Coinciding with his move to Barcelona, Davies acquired a [[Ugandan passport]], because under the [[Cotonou Agreement]] African players are not subject to the same limited quotas in the [[Liga ACB]] as American players.<ref name="cotonou">{{multiref|
{{cite news |last1=Aragón |first1=Andrés |title=La liga ACB con menos jugadores españoles de la historia: sólo el 30% |url=https://www.elmundo.es/deportes/baloncesto/liga-endesa/2019/10/15/5da335b0fdddff9b788b45ae.html |access-date=10 March 2022 |work=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]] |location=Madrid |date=15 October 2019 |language=es |quote=Coincidiendo con su fichaje por el Barcelona, Brandon Davies se comprometió a jugar un par de amistosos con Uganda para obtener el pasaporte cotonou y no ocupar plaza de extracomunitario. }}|
{{cite web |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/es/acb-es/918846/brandon-davies-no-ocupara-plaza-de-extracomunitario/ |title=Brandon Davies no ocupará plaza de extracomunitario |date=13 August 2019 |language=es |quote=Uganda es uno de los 78 países de África, el Caribe y el Pacífico integrados en el acuerdo ‘cotonou’ y, por tanto, el ex pívot del Zalgiris no ocupará plaza de extracomunitario.  |access-date=10 March 2022 |work=eurohoops.net }}
}}</ref> As part of the arrangement, Barcelona agreed to release Davies to play some matches for the [[Uganda men's national basketball team|Uganda national team]],<ref name="cotonou"/> and in November 2021 he played in three [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Africa)#Group A|2023 World Cup qualifiers]] in [[Benguela]].<ref>{{cite web |title=African Qualifiers; Players; Brandon DAVIES |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/african-qualifiers/player/Brandon-Davies |website=FIBA Basketball World Cup 2023 |publisher=FIBA |access-date=10 March 2022 |language=en}}</ref> (The [[Turkey men's national basketball team|Turkey team]] complained that Barcelona had not released [[Sertaç Şanlı]] for [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)#Group B 2|its qualifiers]] in Europe.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Molina |first1=Alex |title=Brandon Davies brilla con Uganda en plena polémica por las ventanas |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/es/fiba-world-cup-es/1276352/brandon-davies-brilla-con-uganda-en-plena-polemica-por-las-ventanas/ |access-date=10 March 2022 |work=Eurohoops |date=28 November 2021 |language=es}}</ref>)

==Personal life==
Davies is a member of [[the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.theroot.com/articles/culture/2014/06/jabari_parker_becomes_first_black_mormon_in_the_nba.html |title=''The Root'' article on Parker draft |access-date=2014-08-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808052445/http://www.theroot.com/articles/culture/2014/06/jabari_parker_becomes_first_black_mormon_in_the_nba.html |archive-date=2014-08-08 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[https://keepingscore.blogs.time.com/2011/03/04/brandon-davies-is-byus-premarital-sex-controversy-good-for-college-sports/ Brandon Davies: Is BYU’s Premarital Sex Controversy Good For College Sports?]</ref> He had a son with Jayci Underwood in 2011, that has been adopted since birth. He married Lenzie Quist of Riverside, California, in January 2015. They have a daughter, born in the summer of 2016.
